source.title: Samsung is testing a feature that changes the angle of photos you’ve already taken
source.text: Android Authority found code in the beta for One UI 9.5 referring to a feature called Recompose that might let you change the angle of a photo after you've taken it. The code is part of Samsung's Photo Editor app and builds on the existing Move tool. Users would be able to toggle between Move and Recompose, the latter of which is associated with text strings reading: Drag with one finger to change the perspective. Use two fingers to pan, zoom, and rotate. And: Move this slider to make background objects appear closer or farther away. Samsung is testing a feature that lets you change the camera angle of a photo after you’ve already taken it.

Code found in the One UI 9.5 beta shows a new tool called Recompose. It allows you to drag one finger to shift perspective and use a slider to move background objects closer or farther away. The tool builds on the existing Move tool inside Samsung’s Photo Editor app.

Does shifting the perspective of a photo make it feel less real?

draft.instagram_caption:
Samsung is testing a way to change the camera angle of a photo after you’ve already taken it.

New code found in the One UI 9.5 beta reveals a tool called Recompose. Unlike a simple crop, this tool lets you drag one finger to change the perspective of the shot. You can also use a slider to make objects in the background appear closer or farther away.

The feature is part of the Samsung Photo Editor app and expands on the existing Move tool. It uses pan, zoom, and rotate controls to give users more control over a finished image.
